title: Ten-person planning workshop
lines: Good afternoon, everyone. This is the steering committee for the office move, and we have six items today. Let's start with the timeline.
The landlord has confirmed we can get the keys on the first of February. The fit-out will take about eight weeks after that.
So we'd move in at the start of April?
Early April, yes, assuming the council approves the plans for the kitchen and the bathrooms.
When do we expect the council decision?
They said four to six weeks. We submitted the plans last Monday.
Okay. Olivia, what does that mean for the lease on the current office?
Our current lease ends on the thirty first of March. We can extend month to month, but the rent goes up by twenty percent.
Twenty percent is steep. Is that negotiable?
I've asked. They'll come back to me next week. Worst case, one extra month costs us about nine thousand dollars.
Let's plan for one extra month as a contingency, and hope we don't need it.
Can I raise the network setup? That's the thing most likely to delay us.
The building has fibre, but the provider needs ten weeks' notice to connect us. If we order it after the keys, we'll miss April.
Can we order it before we have the keys?
Yes, if the landlord signs the access form. I sent it to them on Tuesday, but I haven't heard back.
I'll chase the landlord tomorrow. I'm meeting their property manager anyway.
Thanks, Frank. If we get the form signed this week, we're fine.
Good. Next item, furniture. Thandi, you were collecting quotes.
I have three quotes. The cheapest is forty two thousand, and the one I'd recommend is fifty one thousand, because it includes installation.
The desks are the same. The recommended one has better chairs and a five year warranty, instead of two years.
Then I think the extra cost is worth it, especially with the installation included.
I agree. Installation alone would cost us five or six thousand otherwise.
Any objections to going with the fifty one thousand dollar quote?
Then that's decided. Thandi, please accept that quote and ask for delivery in the last week of March.
Will do. I'll send the purchase order to finance by Wednesday.
Next, the seating plan. James, you were going to survey the teams.
Yes. About seventy percent of people want to keep fixed desks, and thirty percent are happy to hot desk.
The sales team wants to sit near the meeting rooms, and the engineers want the quiet corner away from the kitchen.
That seems reasonable. Can you draft a seating plan for the next meeting?
I can have a first draft by the twentieth of January.
Great. Olivia, the budget. Where do we stand overall?
The approved budget is three hundred and twenty thousand. With the furniture decision, we've committed two hundred and ninety.
That leaves thirty thousand for contingencies, which is a bit thin given the lease risk.
The fit-out quote also has a ten percent allowance for surprises, so we have some cushion there.
Okay. Let's keep an eye on it, and report back if the contingency drops below twenty thousand.
One open question from my side. Are we keeping the old furniture, or selling it?
Good question. I don't think we've decided.
Some of it could go to the Sydney office. They asked for desks last year.
Let's find out what Sydney actually needs before we decide. Can someone ask them?
I'll ask the Sydney office manager this week.
Thank you. Last item, communication to staff. I'd like to send an update before Christmas.
I can write the first draft, and include the seating survey results.
Perfect. Let me summarise the actions. Frank chases the landlord about the fibre access form tomorrow.
Thandi accepts the furniture quote, sends the purchase order by Wednesday, and asks Sydney about the old furniture.
James drafts the seating plan by the twentieth of January and writes the staff update. Olivia follows up on the lease extension next week.
And Raj orders the fibre as soon as the form is signed.
Great. Thanks everyone. We'll meet again in two weeks.
Morning everyone. Let's get started, we've got a lot to cover before the launch. Raj, do you want to begin with the release status?
Sure. The release candidate went out to the beta group on Monday. We've had about three hundred people install it so far.
Crash rates are low, under half a percent, but there's one issue with the sync on older tablets that we need to fix.
How serious is the tablet issue?
It only happens when the battery saver is on. The sync stops in the background and doesn't resume until you open the app.
That sounds like the background limits changed in the last system update.
Yes, exactly, that's our theory too. I think we can work around it, but it'll take a few days.
Okay. Is that a blocker for the launch on the twentieth?
I don't think so. It affects maybe two percent of users, and they don't lose any data. It just syncs later.
From the support side, I'd rather we ship with a known issue than delay. We can put a note in the help centre.
Agreed. Let's keep the launch date of October the twentieth, and treat the tablet sync as a fast follow.
Okay, I'll plan the fix for the first patch release.
James, where are we on the marketing assets?
The landing page is done and the screenshots are being updated this week. The launch video is the one I'm worried about.
The agency sent the first cut yesterday and it uses the old onboarding screens. They need the new ones from design.
If they get the new screens by Thursday, they can still deliver the final version by the fifteenth.
Who owns getting them the screens?
That's me. I'll get the exported screens from the design team and send them over by Thursday.
Great. Niamh, how is support preparing for the launch?
We've written twelve new help articles, and the team has done two training sessions on the new features.
My main concern is staffing. Last launch, our ticket volume tripled in the first week.
Do we have extra people lined up?
Two people from the sales team volunteered to help with the chat queue. I'd like one more, ideally someone technical.
I could lend you one of the engineers for the first three days. Maybe Tom, he knows the sync code really well.
That would be brilliant, thank you.
Good. Raj, can you confirm with Tom this week?
Next, budget. We're about fifteen thousand dollars over on the launch budget, mostly because of the video.
Some of that is the reshoot. The original agency quote didn't include the second day of filming.
Can we cover it from the events budget? The conference in December was cancelled.
I think so, but finance needs to approve moving the money.
Then I'll raise it with finance on Friday. If they say no, we'll cut the paid social campaign instead.
Can I ask one question about the launch day itself? Are we doing the announcement in the morning or the afternoon?
That's not decided yet. The press team wants the morning, but our users are mostly in the US, so the afternoon might be better.
From an engineering view, the morning is better. If something goes wrong, we have the whole day to fix it.
That's a fair point. Let's leave it open for now, and I'll decide with the press team by Monday.
Okay, let me summarise. Launch stays on the twentieth. Raj fixes the tablet sync in the first patch and confirms Tom for support.
James sends the new screens to the agency by Thursday. I'll talk to finance on Friday and decide the announcement time by Monday.
And I'll publish the help articles the day before launch.
Perfect. Thanks everyone, same time next week.
Thanks for making time, James. I wanted to go through the cloud hosting renewal before the end of the month.
Sure. I had a look at the quote they sent on Friday. It's about eighteen percent higher than last year.
That's more than I expected. Did they explain where the increase comes from?
Mostly storage. Our backups have doubled since March, and they've moved us onto a new pricing tier.
The compute part is actually a little cheaper, because we committed to reserved instances last spring.
Okay. So if we cleaned up the old backups, how much of that would we save?
Probably a third of the increase. We keep ninety days of snapshots, and nobody has restored anything older than two weeks.
Then let's cut the retention to thirty days. Can you check with the security team that thirty days still meets the audit requirements?
Yes, I'll ask Priya today. She did the last audit, so she'll know.
Great. And what about the alternative provider? Did you get a number from them?
I did. They're about ten percent cheaper on paper, but the migration would take at least six weeks of engineering time.
Six weeks is a lot. We don't have that before the product launch in November.
Exactly. My suggestion is to renew for one year, not three, and revisit the move in the spring.
I agree. Let's renew for one year. I'll sign the contract once the retention change is confirmed.
The other thing I wanted to talk about is hiring. How are the interviews for the platform engineer going?
We've had four candidates so far. Two were strong, and one of them, Marco, has done exactly this kind of migration before.
That would be useful if we do move providers next year.
That's what I thought. I'd like to bring him in for the final round next week, if you can join.
I can do Tuesday or Thursday afternoon. Wednesday is full of budget meetings.
Let's say Thursday at two. I'll send the invite and the take-home task results.
Perfect. Is there anything blocking you that I can help with?
Just one thing. The finance team still hasn't approved the monitoring tool we asked for in August.
I'll chase that with Daniel in finance. I think it's stuck because the request went to the wrong cost centre.
Okay, so to recap. You'll confirm the thirty day retention with Priya, and send me the updated quote by Friday.
Yes. And I'll set up the final interview with Marco for Thursday at two.
And I'll sort out the monitoring tool approval. Thanks, James, that was really helpful.
